verdict.rationale: Calendly can be driven headlessly through its REST API v2. Personal access tokens give non-interactive auth for internal automation, and the API supports programmatic booking and read/write of scheduling data. Webhook subscriptions (with signing keys) support event-driven pipelines. However, there is no first-party CLI or CI-specific tooling, so automation means writing custom API scripts. Missing for 10: an official CLI or CI integration, documented CI/headless usage examples, and independent hands-on corroboration of automated pipelines.
